rows.grounds: compound epithet: deva-deva (god of gods) + aṅga (limb/body) + sukhinī (happy, delighting in); feminine nominative singular describing the goddess
compound epithet: deva-deva (god of gods) + aṅga (limb/body) + vāsinī (dwelling in, residing in); feminine nominative singular describing the goddess

items.question: In what ways is the goddess intimately united with the body of the god of gods?
premises: The goddess delights in the limbs of the god of gods.
The goddess dwells within the limbs of the god of gods.
These epithets express her intimate union with the supreme deity.
items.inference: The goddess is both joyfully present in and resident within the body of the god of gods.
uncertainties: Whether aṅga refers specifically to physical limbs or more broadly to the body or aspects of the deity.
items.plain_english: She who delights in the limbs of the god of gods, and she who dwells in the limbs of the god of gods.
